samples.question: This picture is a small transit map. Each dark disc is a station, and each coloured stroke is part of a transit line: there are exactly four lines, one blue, one orange, one purple and one teal. A line runs through the stations it touches, and once you board a line you may ride it to any station on that same line for free. You may switch from one line to another only at a station where both of those lines stop. The green disc is the station you start at and the red disc is the station you must reach; both are ordinary stations apart from their colour. Count only the switches from one line to another, not the stations you pass and not the lines you ride. Travelling from the green station to the red station, what is the smallest number of line switches you can manage with? Answer 1, 2, or 3.
